newsitem.title: INDIA: India bullion down on weak global trends.
newsitem.headline: India bullion down on weak global trends.

text.p: Gold 24 carat opened 5 rupees lower at 4,445 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,450 rupees amid sluggish physical demand while a weak trend in world prices prompted fresh offerings, dealer said.

Prices of a gold biscuit (116.64 gramme) opened steady at 52,000 rupees per piece in limited activity during early trade. They were down by 100 rupees on Tuesday while the market was closed on Wednesday for a Hindu feast.
"Gold remained subdued in early trade but may bounce back later in the day looking at the hike in the premiums of import licences," one broker said.
"This premium has gone up to 13.40/13.50 percent from 12 percent which in turn has lifted lending cost of the imported gold," he said.

Silver (.999) opened 65 rupees lower at 6,210 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,275 rupees on higher supplies of the imported metal while fresh losses in the world market prompted unloading by local stockists. Silver was down 45 rupees on Tuesday and the market was closed on Wednesday.
Sentiment was subdued as industrial buyers sat on the sidelines and volume was thin in early trade.
